SG-B — THE LEDGER LINE CARRIES NO TIMESTAMP, so §7.3's 'token throughput' has no wall clock. §4.4 (plan:1680-1684) enumerates the line's fields and none of them is a time of day; 11.7's promoted rows add none. Adding one would change a line shape another promoted spec has already pinned. RESOLUTION: throughput is reported as `completionTokensPerUpstreamSecond` = sum(completionTokens) / (sum(upstreamMs) / 1000) over records where BOTH are non-null, null when that denominator is 0 — generation throughput per second of upstream time, which is the number that is actually derivable and is the one the POC's cost dataset wants. SG-C — CUMULATIVE VS WINDOWED, decided rather than left to the implementer. assertions.text: DOCTEST (router/tests/dashboard_test.cpp, RED first as a compile failure — `dashboard/ledger_view.hpp` does not exist): `conductor::dashboard::parseLedgerLine(std::string_view) -> std::optional<LedgerRecord>` is a pure, non-throwing decode of ONE ledger line. A line carrying the full 11.7 key set decodes field for field into `LedgerRecord{ std::string model; std::optional<std::string> role; std::optional<std::string> group; std::string priority; std::optional<std::int64_t> queueWaitMs; std::optional<std::int64_t> upstreamMs; std::optional<std::int64_t> promptTokens; std::optional<std::int64_t> completionTokens; std::optional<bool> schemaMissing; std::optional<bool> schemaConformed; int status; }` — JSON null decodes to a disengaged optional for every optional field (role, group, queueWaitMs, upstreamMs, promptTokens, completionTokens, schemaMissing, schemaConformed), an empty-string `model` stays an empty string rather than becoming an error, and `priority` is the resolved class string verbatim. The opaque `timings` value is IGNORED (the dashboard never reads it) and any UNKNOWN key is ignored rather than rejected, so a later 11.7 field addition cannot break the reader. `std::nullopt` — never an exception, never a partially-filled record — is returned for: an empty line, a whitespace-only line, a truncated line that is not valid JSON, valid JSON that is not an object (a bare number, a string, an array), an object missing `status`, and an object whose `status` is a string rather than a number. parseLedgerLine has no state: parsing the same line twice yields equal records.

DOCTEST: `class LedgerTail` turns an arbitrarily-chunked byte stream into whole records without ever parsing a half-written line — the file is appended to by a live router (11.7 flushes per line, appends only, never rewrites), so a read can land mid-line. `LedgerTail::consume(std::string_view) -> std::vector<LedgerRecord>` emits a record ONLY for a line terminated by '\n'. Feeding one complete line in a single chunk emits one record; feeding that same line split at an arbitrary byte offset across two consume() calls emits ZERO records from the first call and exactly that one record from the second; feeding three complete lines as one chunk emits three records in file order; feeding two-and-a-half lines emits exactly two records and the half is carried, then completed by the next chunk. A chunk that is exactly '\n' after a carried complete line emits that line. Records are always emitted in file order, and the total emitted across any chunking of the same byte sequence is identical to the total emitted when that sequence is consumed as one chunk. A trailing '\r' before the newline is stripped before parsing so a CRLF-terminated line decodes identically.

DOCTEST (G5 applied to the reader): no malformed input can stop the tail or crash the viewer. A complete line that parseLedgerLine rejects is SKIPPED — consume() emits nothing for it, increments `LedgerTail::skipped()`, and continues to emit records for every well-formed line before and after it in the same chunk (asserted with a 3-line chunk whose middle line is truncated JSON: two records out, skipped()==1). Blank lines are skipped WITHOUT incrementing skipped() (they are not corruption). A carried partial that exceeds the tail's maximum carry (a constructor parameter, default 1 MiB) is DROPPED along with everything up to the next newline, skipped() increments once, and the tail resumes cleanly on the following line — so a single unterminated garbage blob cannot grow the process without bound. `LedgerTail::reset()` discards any carry and leaves skipped() untouched. consume() never throws for any input, including embedded NUL bytes and invalid UTF-8.

DOCTEST: the follow position is computed by a pure function, so the one piece of the tail loop that can lose or duplicate data is testable without a filesystem. `nextRead(std::uint64_t consumedOffset, std::uint64_t currentSize) -> TailStep{ std::uint64_t offset; bool restart; }` returns {consumedOffset, false} when currentSize > consumedOffset (append: read forward from where we stopped), {consumedOffset, false} when currentSize == consumedOffset (nothing new: no re-read of already-consumed bytes, so no record is ever counted twice), and {0, true} when currentSize < consumedOffset — the file was replaced or truncated by a new run, so the whole file is re-read from byte 0 and the caller is told to restart. Fresh start (consumedOffset 0, currentSize 0) is {0, false} with restart false. The function is noexcept and total over all inputs including currentSize 0 with a large consumedOffset.

DOCTEST: `LedgerView::record(const LedgerRecord&)` folds a record into cumulative counters and `LedgerView::aggregate() -> LedgerAggregate` reports them, with EXACT hand-computed values over a fixed record set. `totalRequests` is the number of records recorded. `schemaMissing` and `schemaConformed` are the COUNTS of records whose respective optional holds `true` (a false and a disengaged optional both contribute 0 — the same rule 11.7's endpoint uses). `statusCounts` is keyed by the decimal status rendered as a string, so a set of three 200s and one 503 yields exactly {"200":3,"503":1} and no key is present with value 0. `promptTokens` and `completionTokens` are sums over non-null values only, 0 when no record carries one. Over an empty view, aggregate() returns totalRequests 0, both schema counts 0, an EMPTY statusCounts, both token sums 0. The six field NAMES are byte-identical to the /conductor/metrics aggregate 11.7 serves and to conductor/adapter/router-client.ts:44-51's MetricsSummary, so the TUI and the endpoint cannot quote two different numbers under the same word.

DOCTEST: `waitMsP50` and `waitMsP95` use the SAME nearest-rank definition 11.7's endpoint uses — the sorted queueWaitMs samples at 1-indexed ranks ceil(0.50*N) and ceil(0.95*N) — asserted as EXACT values for a hand-computed sample set (e.g. the ten samples 0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8,100 give p50 == 4 and p95 == 100), and BOTH 0 when N is 0. Records whose queueWaitMs is null contribute no sample and do not change N. Per SG-C the samples are the ones in the bounded recent window, NOT every record ever recorded: with a window of 4 and eight recorded waits, the percentiles are computed over the last four only, which is asserted by recording a set whose windowed percentiles differ from its whole-history percentiles and checking the windowed answer. Sorting is by value and is not disturbed by record order: the same multiset fed in any order yields the same two numbers.

DOCTEST: the two derived ratios are defined at their edges rather than left to divide by zero. `schemaConformanceRate` is `std::optional<double>` = (count of records whose schemaConformed holds true) / (count of records whose schemaConformed is NON-NULL), and is DISENGAGED — not 0.0, not NaN — when that denominator is 0; with two true, one false and five nulls it is exactly 2.0/3.0. `completionTokensPerUpstreamSecond` (SG-B) is `std::optional<double>` = sum(completionTokens) / (sum(upstreamMs) / 1000.0) taken over records where BOTH completionTokens and upstreamMs are non-null, disengaged when the summed upstreamMs over those records is 0 or no such record exists; with two records of (100 tokens, 1000 ms) and (300 tokens, 1000 ms) it is exactly 200.0. Both are cumulative per SG-C. Records missing one half of a pair are excluded from BOTH the numerator and the denominator of the ratio they feed, so a shed 503 line (null tokens, null upstreamMs) never depresses the throughput figure.

DOCTEST: the dashboard is a tail, so folding must be order-robust and chunk-independent. For a fixed sequence of records, feeding them one call at a time and feeding them in arbitrary multi-record batches produce IDENTICAL cumulative aggregates (totalRequests, schemaMissing, schemaConformed, statusCounts, promptTokens, completionTokens, schemaConformanceRate, completionTokensPerUpstreamSecond) — asserted by building two LedgerView instances and comparing every field. The bounded window preserves ARRIVAL ORDER regardless of batching: `window()` returns the retained records in the order they were recorded, oldest first. No aggregate field depends on the number of consume()/record() calls used to deliver the same records.

DOCTEST (bounded memory in a process meant to run all day): `LedgerView` is constructed with a window size (default 200) and retains at most that many records. After recording windowSize + K records for K > 0, `window()` holds EXACTLY windowSize entries and they are the LAST windowSize recorded, in order; the oldest are dropped, not the newest. The cumulative counters are unaffected by eviction — totalRequests equals windowSize + K, and the token sums and statusCounts still include the evicted records — so the summary pane keeps counting a long run while memory stays flat. A window size of 1 retains exactly the most recent record. The lanes and affinity summary are computed over the retained window only, so an evicted record contributes to neither.

DOCTEST (the file-replacement path SG-D/`nextRead` restart feeds): `LedgerView::restart()` returns the view to its constructed state — aggregate() reports totalRequests 0, both schema counts 0, an empty statusCounts, zero token sums, both percentiles 0 and both optional ratios disengaged; window() is empty; lanes() and affinity() report their empty-set values. Recording after restart() counts from zero, so a router restart that replaces metrics.jsonl produces a dashboard reading for the NEW run and never a total spanning two files. restart() is idempotent (calling it twice equals calling it once) and is legal on a never-recorded view. This mirrors 11.7's own rule that the aggregate is process-lifetime state and never a re-read of the file (11.7 row 11.7-aggregate-in-memory) — the dashboard's counters are likewise a fold over what it has SEEN, and it makes no attempt to reconstruct history it did not tail.

DOCTEST (SG-A, the 'in-flight/queue lanes' pane made from what the ledger actually carries): `LedgerView::lanes() -> std::vector<Lane>` where `Lane{ std::string group; std::int64_t completed; std::int64_t queued; std::int64_t shed; std::int64_t waitMsP95; }`. One lane per DISTINCT group value in the retained window, plus at most one lane for untagged records whose `group` field is the empty string. Lanes are ordered by FIRST APPEARANCE in the window (stable and jitter-free — never by count, which would make the pane jump between frames). Per lane: `completed` is the number of records in the window carrying that group; `queued` is how many of them have a non-null queueWaitMs strictly greater than 0 (they waited behind a full pool); `shed` is how many have status 503; `waitMsP95` is the nearest-rank p95 over that lane's non-null queueWaitMs samples, 0 when it has none. An empty window yields an empty vector. A window of records that are all untagged yields exactly one lane with an empty group name. The sum of every lane's `completed` equals window().size().

DOCTEST (SG-G, the group-affinity marker): `LedgerView::affinity() -> AffinitySummary{ std::int64_t taggedRequests; std::int64_t runs; std::int64_t longestRun; std::int64_t contiguousFollowers; std::optional<double> hitRate; }` computed over the retained window IN LEDGER ORDER. A RUN is a maximal block of CONSECUTIVE window positions all carrying the same non-empty group; an untagged record between two same-group records SPLITS the run (it is a position in the sequence, not a gap to be ignored). `taggedRequests` is the count of records with a non-empty group; `runs` is the number of blocks; `longestRun` is the largest block length (0 when there are no tagged records); `contiguousFollowers` equals taggedRequests - runs, i.e. every tagged record that immediately followed a record of its own group. `hitRate` is contiguousFollowers / taggedRequests, DISENGAGED when taggedRequests is 0. Worked cases asserted exactly: [A,A,A] -> tagged 3, runs 1, longest 3, followers 2, rate 2/3; [A,B,A,B] -> tagged 4, runs 4, longest 1, followers 0, rate 0.0; [A,A,untagged,A] -> tagged 3, runs 2, longest 2, followers 1, rate 1/3; all-untagged -> tagged 0, runs 0, longest 0, followers 0, rate disengaged.

DOCTEST (what keeps main.cpp a THIN adapter — G3's spirit applied to Branch B: every string the TUI prints for the summary pane is produced by a pure function, so the formatting is under test and ftxui renders pre-formatted text). `summaryRows(const LedgerAggregate&) -> std::vector<std::pair<std::string,std::string>>` returns EXACTLY these label/value pairs in EXACTLY this order: "requests", "status counts", "prompt tokens", "completion tokens", "wait p50 ms", "wait p95 ms", "schema missing", "schema conformed", "schema conformance", "tokens/s upstream". Integers render as plain decimal with no separators. "status counts" renders as space-separated `<status>:<count>` pairs in ASCENDING NUMERIC status order ("200:3 503:1"), and as "-" when statusCounts is empty.
